mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Company Registry in the Investor's Home Jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the home jurisdiction is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention (e.g., Germany, UK, France), obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority (e.g., Federal Office of Justice in Germany, Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in UK). If the home jurisdiction is not a member (e.g., Canada, UAE), obtain consular legalization from the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that jurisdiction. The document must be notarized locally before apostille/consularization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or Certificate of Existence) of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registry or Equivalent Authority in the Investor's Home Jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same as above: Apostille for Hague Convention members; consular legalization for non-members. The certificate must be issued within 30 days of submission to the Chinese authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney Authorizing the Formation of the JV
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The resolution must be notarized by a local notary public, then apostilled (if the home jurisdiction is a Hague member) or consularized (if not). The resolution must explicitly authorize the signatory to execute the JV contract and related documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or Memorandum and Articles) of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign Investor's Corporate Secretary or Legal Representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the copy, then apostille or consularize as per the home jurisdiction's status. The document must be certified as a true copy by the issuing entity.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be notarized, then apostilled or consularized. The letter should confirm the investor's financial standing and account history, and must be dated within 90 days of submission.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of the foreign investor must undergo mandatory screening against the following lists: (1) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List (UNSC), (2) the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN), (3) the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (4) the UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, and (5) the People's Bank of China (PBOC) and Ministry of Public Security (MPS) domestic sanctions and PEP lists. Screening must be conducted at the time of incorporation and on a continuous basis (at least quarterly) using a risk-based approach. For PEPs, enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required, including source of wealth and source of funds verification. Any positive match or red flag must be escalated to the AML Compliance Officer and may result in rejection of the application. The screening process must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and Online Name Clearance Portal (https://www.gsxt.gov.cn)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Chinese characters. For foreign investors, the name may include a phonetic transliteration of the foreign name, but the official registered name must be in Chinese. The name must follow the four-tier structure: (1) Administrative division (e.g., city or province), (2) Trade name (unique and not identical to existing names), (3) Industry or business characteristics (e.g., 'Data Labeling' or 'AI Training'), and (4) Company type (e.g., 'Co., Ltd.'). Pinyin transliteration is permitted for the trade name but must be clearly distinguishable from existing names. The name must not contain any characters that are misleading or violate public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the SAMR within 15 working days of the rejection notice. The appeal must be submitted in writing, stating the grounds for reconsideration and providing evidence that the name complies with all statutory requirements. The SAMR must issue a decision within 30 working days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the People's Court within 6 months. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a new name application with a revised trade name, ensuring it is distinct and not on the prohibited list. The name reservation can be extended once for an additional 30 days by filing a request before the expiration date, subject to payment of a nominal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture. The registered office must be a physical address within the jurisdiction where the JV is incorporated, and it must be the actual place of business. Tax authorities and banks require a physical presence for verification, and the JV must have a lease agreement or property ownership certificate. The use of a registered agent for service of process is allowed, but the registered office itself must be a physical location. Failure to maintain a physical office may result in deregistration and penalties.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspections: (1) Verify that the office is staffed during business hours; (2) Confirm that the company name is displayed on the door or reception area; (3) Ensure that lease agreements and utility bills are available; (4) Check that business records and seals are kept on-site; (5) Verify that the registered address matches the actual location. Risk assessment: Moderate to High, especially within the first year of incorporation. Municipal tax authorities and SAMR conduct random inspections, and the likelihood increases if the company is flagged for any compliance issues. The JV must maintain a physical presence and be prepared for inspections at any time.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee is charged for the initial registration; however, a stamp duty of 0.05% of registered capital may apply (capped at CNY 500,000).

Notarization of foreign investor documents (certificate of incorporation, good standing, board resolution, articles, bank letter)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notary fees, typically USD 100-200 per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs) or Chinese Embassy/Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Apostille fees vary by country (e.g., USD 10-50 per document); consular legalization fees are typically USD 50-100 per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees for drafting JV contract, Articles of Association, and corporate governance documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for cross-border JV formation, typically USD 2,500-5,000.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office lease deposit (first month rent and security deposit)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for commercial office space in a Tier-1 city, typically USD 1,000-3,000 per month.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation and certification of documents into Chinese
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate, typically USD 50-100 per page.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 29-32, 47-50, 68-69, and 91; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020); Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Company Registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the local Market Supervision Administration in the city where the registered office is located; foreign investment registration windows and the SAMR enterprise registration online portal handle the filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Company Establishment Registration Application form (with unified social credit code application) submitted via the SAMR online enterprise registration portal or physical market supervision window.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement apply to a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture engaged in ISIC 8220 AI data labeling and BPO. Under the PRC Company Law, shareholders determine the registered capital in the articles of association, must pay the full subscribed amount within five years after incorporation, and may contribute in cash or lawful non-cash assets. The subscribed capital is not subject to a government escrow, but the contribution must be paid into the company's own bank account and recorded in the company's capital contribution ledger. Any regulatory minimum would arise only if the company later adds a licensed physical activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION - [COMPANY NAME]. Upon lawful convening of the first meeting of the Board of Directors, held at the registered office on [date], with all directors present, waiver of notice duly executed, a chairman elected, and a quorum confirmed, the directors unanimously adopted the following resolutions. 1. Registered Capital and Share Subscription: RESOLVED that the registered capital of the Company be established in the amount of RMB [amount], divided into [number] ordinary registered shares, each of RMB [par value], all subscribed by the founding shareholders in accordance with the shareholders' agreement and articles of association dated [date]; RESOLVED FURTHER that the contribution schedule, form of contribution, including cash or lawful non-cash assets, and the respective rights and obligations of each shareholder be ratified, and that the Board instruct the general manager to ensure that every contribution is verified, paid into the Company's bank account, and recorded in the statutory capital contribution ledger before any share certificate is issued. 2. Registered Office: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [complete address] within the jurisdiction of the Market Supervision Administration and that such address be deemed the Company's statutory seat, repository of its minute books, share register, seal records, and accounting documents; RESOLVED FURTHER that the legal representative and the general manager be jointly authorized to execute and deliver an office lease, obtain landlord consent certificates, and file all postal, municipal, and utility registrations. 3. Statutory Officers: RESOLVED that [name] be appointed as the legal representative and Chairperson of the Board; [name] as General Manager and chief executive officer; [name] as supervisor, with the powers and duties prescribed in the PRC Company Law; and [name] as Company Secretary and chief compliance officer; RESOLVED FURTHER that each officer accepts office and that the supervisor shall not simultaneously serve as director or general manager as required by law. 4. Banking Authorization: RESOLVED that the Company maintain its principal bank accounts at [bank and branch], including one basic deposit account in RMB and one foreign currency current account; RESOLVED that the Chairperson, General Manager, and finance manager be authorized, any two acting jointly, to sign bank account opening forms, cheques, remittance instructions, payment orders, and online banking records, to submit KYC forms, and to operate the accounts in accordance with the Company's dual-signature payment authorization matrix. 5. General Authorization: RESOLVED that all directors and officers take all steps necessary for filing with the Market Supervision Administration, tax authority, statistical authority, social insurance bureau, public security body, and other government offices; RESOLVED that the common seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal be adopted and placed in the custody of the compliance officer, and used only in compliance with the internal seal control policy. These resolutions are effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-approval and Foreign Investment Name Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration through the SAMR enterprise name pre-registration online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the enterprise name pre-registration application through the online portal operated by the local Market Supervision Administration under the State Administration for Market Regulation. Select a unique name consisting of administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristics, and company type. Include the proposed registered capital, proposed business scope, shareholder identities, and registered address. The system automatically checks for identical or similar names, prohibited words, and public-interest conflicts. If approved, download the name pre-approval notice; this notice reserves the name for a fixed period, usually six months, and is required for the subsequent establishment filing.
required_dossiers: Enterprise name pre-registration application form
Proposed name list in Chinese and English transliteration
Passport or business license of each founding shareholder
Authorized representative appointment and identity proof
Certificate of incorporation and good standing of foreign corporate shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or prohibited wording, file a new application with up to three alternative distinctive names within 10 working days. If refused because the proposed business scope does not match the name's industry characteristics, revise the scope to reflect ISIC 8220 data labeling, information technology services, and data processing, then resubmit. An administrative reconsideration or, ultimately, judicial review is available under the PRC Administrative Reconsideration Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public office for shareholder signatures and foreign documents, and the establishment filing desk of the Market Supervision Administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Chinese-language Articles of Association and shareholders' agreement before the shareholders and any required notary. These instruments must set out the name and address of each shareholder, subscribed and paid-up registered capital, form and time limit of capital contribution, composition and quorum of the board, powers of the legal representative and general manager, distribution policy, dissolution triggers, and governing law. The foreign investor's corporate authorizations must be legalized by apostille or consular legalization and accompanied by certified copies of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and board resolution. If the original shareholder documents are not in Chinese, submit certified Chinese translations with the application.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association in Chinese
Shareholders' agreement in Chinese and English
Passport or license copies of all shareholders
Power of attorney for local agent
Legalized board resolution of foreign shareholder
Certificate of good standing or equivalent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Market Supervision Administration queries execution, notarization, or translation, cure by obtaining a supplementary notarial certificate or a sworn translation within 15 working days. If the articles of association contain a business scope outside permitted categories, amend and re-execute the articles, then resubmit. If a signature is denied, arrange a personal appearance or digital signing certificate for the shareholder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment Registration and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Market Supervision Administration (enterprise registration window or SAMR online portal) in the district where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic or paper establishment registration application using the pre-approved name and completed statutory instruments. Attach the lease or ownership certificate for the registered office, identity documents of the legal representative, directors, supervisor, general manager, and the shareholders' qualification documents. The application must be signed by the legal representative; an electronic signature through the SAMR portal is accepted. The authority reviews the lawfulness of the capital schedule, business scope, prohibited activities, and governance documents. No statutory registration fee is charged. Upon approval, the authority issues the business license and unified social credit code, at which point the company acquires legal personality and may commence administrative operations.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Company Establishment Registration Application form
Name pre-approval notice
Articles of Association and shareholders' agreement
Certificate of registered office (lease or property ownership certificate)
Identity certificates of legal representative, directors, supervisor and manager
Shareholder qualification documents with legalization
Feasibility study or business plan if required by local registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or denied on grounds of an ineffective registered address or an impermissible capital schedule, cure by substituting a compliant business premise or amending the articles of association, then respond to the authority's written query within the statutory 15-day period. If the denial persists, file an administrative reconsideration or bring an administrative lawsuit. A second application with corrected documentation may also be filed without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Social Insurance, Seal and Bank Account Integration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal tax service bureau, human resources and social security bureau, licensed bank, licensed seal engraver, and public security bureau seal-record office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the business license, complete the mandatory post-registration integrations within the legal deadlines. Register with the municipal tax authority through the electronic tax bureau, complete social insurance and payroll registration for employees, file statistical declarations, and open a basic deposit account at a licensed commercial bank. Engrave the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal only at a licensed engraving shop, then submit seal impressions and file the seal record at the local public security bureau. Apply for electronic invoice quota and, where applicable, VAT general taxpayer status; set up monthly accounting and payroll reporting. Open a foreign exchange account for foreign investor capital contributions and future dividend repatriation.
required_dossiers: Business license and unified social credit code certificate
Legal representative identity certificate
Articles of Association and share contribution verification
Office lease and landlord property certificate
Bank account opening forms and KYC documents
Social insurance registration forms
Seal engraving record and public security bureau seal-filing receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is queried because the office lacks a physical presence, submit the lease invoice, utility bill, and landlord certificate to verify the address. If bank KYC rejects due to source-of-funds ambiguity, provide bank statements or source declarations of the shareholders and resubmit or apply at another licensed bank. If the seal-recording authority queries custody, amend the seal control policy and provide the new custodian's authorization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Environmental Licensing Applicability Determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Not Applicable for industrial licensing; for standard office compliance the local Fire and Rescue Brigade and the workplace safety authority may inspect the registered premises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct the industrial and environmental licensing assessment for the registered business. ISIC 8220 AI data labeling, bounding-box annotation, and RLHF data curation is a pure digital and consulting/BPO service; it does not constitute manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing, and therefore no industrial operating permit, Environmental Impact Assessment, or Civil Defense industrial fire license is required. The Company should nonetheless obtain a routine commercial fire safety inspection certificate for the office premises, adopt workplace safety rules, and, if data labeling involves personal information, complete a Personal Information Protection Law impact assessment. The business license scope must expressly cover data processing, software services, and information technology services.
required_dossiers: Commercial office fire safety inspection certificate (routine lease clearance)
Personal information impact assessment, if applicable
Labor contract and workplace safety policy templates
Business license with data-processing service scope
Office floor plan and emergency evacuation plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire safety inspection certificate is queried, remedy any structural, egress, or extinguisher deficiencies and re-inspect. If the personal information impact assessment is flagged, revise the data processing records, appoint a responsible officer, and resubmit to the competent protection authority. If the business scope does not mention data processing or information technology services, amend the articles and update the company registration through the Market Supervision Administration before commencing client contracts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing board is engaged for ISIC 8220 services; standard office fire-safety oversight sits with the local Fire and Rescue Brigade and workplace safety oversight with the Emergency Management Bureau.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operating permit is required; the company operates under its SAMR business license and service registrations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment and provincial Ecology and Environment Department (not engaged for this service-only venture)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - pure digital/BPO service under ISIC 8220; no Environmental Registration, EIA Report, or Full EIA is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, VOC, hazardous-waste, or stack-emission discharge points exist at the registered office. General office waste and e-waste disposal obligations apply under local municipal waste regulations if computing hardware is replaced.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial Civil Defense permit. Routine commercial fire-safety inspection of the office premises under the PRC Fire Protection Law and standard occupational safety obligations under the Work Safety Law for office and IT workstations apply; these are normal lease and employer clearances, not a project-specific operating license.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), operating the National Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax Bureau) online taxpayer portal accessible via the STA official website and provincial STA e-taxation portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: After SAMR incorporation, the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is issued an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code on its PRC business license; this code is the statutory taxpayer identification number for corporate income tax, VAT, and other national taxes. Step 2: Within 30 days of business license issuance, the JV completes taxpayer registration with the competent local STA office through the e-Tax Bureau, submitting the business license, articles of association, registered address proof, legal representative identity documents, and board resolution appointing finance/tax personnel. Step 3: The JV completes indirect tax status registration: it must register for VAT, choose between small-scale taxpayer and general taxpayer status (general status is compulsory when rolling 12-month taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000), open an electronic invoice account, obtain tax-control digital credentials, and bind the account to the STA e-invoice platform. Step 4: The JV registers for payroll individual income tax withholding and social insurance. Step 5: For any foreign non-resident enterprise that is the overseas parent or beneficial owner of China-source income (dividends, interest, royalties, fees) but maintains no PRC establishment, the JV as statutory withholding agent completes non-resident withholding tax registration through the e-Tax Bureau; the non-resident uses its home-country TIN where available, or is assigned an STA-issued temporary tax identification number for Chinese withholding filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification: the PRC taxes resident Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures at entity level as a domestic enterprise; there is no check-the-box, limited-liability look-through, or hybrid-mismatch election. Administrative elections available are VAT-related: the small-scale/general taxpayer status election before the RMB 5,000,000 mandatory threshold, election of simplified VAT accounting for eligible modern services where permitted, and the zero-rating/exemption classification of cross-border services through the STA cross-border taxable services catalogue.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No annual turnover threshold for basic tax registration; every PRC-incorporated enterprise must register for tax within 30 days of business license issuance. For VAT general taxpayer status, mandatory registration is triggered when taxable turnover in any rolling 12-month period exceeds RMB 5,000,000; below that amount the JV may remain a small-scale taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates real-time digitalized VAT invoicing under the STA Golden Tax Phase IV system and the fully digitalized electronic invoice (e-invoice) platform. The JV must issue special VAT invoices or fully digitalized e-invoices through the STA e-invoice service platform using tax-control digital credentials; high-volume issuers may integrate via API to the platform. Each fully digitalized e-invoice is transmitted to the STA in real time, carries a unique invoice number, a dynamic anti-counterfeiting QR code, and a digital signature; no physical stamping is required and invoice data are cleared by the tax authority at issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available on export of goods where the goods are physically exported from the PRC, the GACC export customs declaration is filed, the exporter retains title/possession evidence, and the export proceeds are collected from the overseas buyer. For cross-border services, a PRC supplier may claim zero-rating or VAT exemption only if the service falls within an STA-recognised cross-border taxable service category (including qualifying data-processing, information technology, software and business-process/BPO services) and the recipient is located outside the PRC, the service is wholly consumed outside the PRC, and the supplier holds contemporaneous contracts, delivery/acceptance evidence, e-invoices, and bank foreign-exchange collection records. In the absence of qualifying export treatment, domestic data-labeling/modern services are generally subject to VAT at the 6% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration Form issued by the General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China (for goods exports; for cross-border services, the formal export service contract and service delivery/acceptance record serve as the export evidence)
Ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing cross-border movement of the goods

Bank foreign-exchange receipt issued by a designated PRC forex bank (the PRC statutory equivalent of an inward remittance certificate) or the State Administration of Foreign Exchange cross-border receipt/payment record confirming repatriation of the export price from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are audited by STA against the e-invoice data, customs export declarations, transport files, and bank foreign-exchange records. If documentation is missing, false, or inconsistent, the STA will claw back the VAT refund or zero-rating benefit and re-instate output VAT, add daily late-payment interest at 0.05%, impose administrative fines of 50% to five times the amount evaded, and may conduct retrospective assessments without statutory limitation where fraud is established. Criminal referral may also be made under the PRC Criminal Law for export-rebate fraud, carrying imprisonment and confiscation of property. Goods or services for which export payment is neither repatriated within the 180-day FX window nor formally registered as deferred collection are treated as non-export sales and assessed VAT with the same penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains current-account convertibility for trade and service payments under IMF Article VIII, but imposes strict capital-account controls. This Sino-foreign equity JV must register all inward direct investment with SAFE through the designated domestic bank before receiving equity capital. Shareholder loans, repatriation of profits, and liquidation proceeds are capital-account items requiring verified documentation and tax clearance; any capital conversion from USD to CNY is settled through the onshore interbank FX market within the daily band. Profit remittances require audited financial statements, corporate income tax return records, a board profit-distribution resolution, and FIE annual report compliance. No de facto free convertibility exists for speculative or unregistered flows, and all FX transactions require underlying true-exposure documentation. Current-account service fees from overseas clients can be received and settled more freely after bank collection verification, but the bank must retain invoices and contractual evidence. This classification means the JV treasury must maintain a segregated capital account for registered equity and separate settlement accounts for operating revenue.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters in China must repatriate overseas current-account proceeds into domestically licensed banks within 180 days from the date of export customs declaration, subject to SAFE verification. There is no mandatory percentage conversion ratio today; after collection, the JV may choose to retain the foreign currency in its settlement account or convert to CNY at the market rate. For services and data-labeling export revenue, the SAFE service trade digital declaration and the applicable service-trade transaction code must be supported by the underlying contract and invoice.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for Foreign-Invested Enterprise Equity
Basic Operational Currency Account and RMB Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and RMB Basic Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability is structurally low for primary treasury use. Wise, PayPal Mass Payout and similar offshore EMI or payment-institution rails are not licensed in China as deposit-taking commercial banks and cannot open corporate settlement accounts that satisfy PBOC account-management rules or SAFE capital-flow reporting. They may serve only as ancillary employee or contractor disbursement conduits through licensed Chinese payment institutions, and must not be used for equity injections, trade-settlement outflows, or repatriation of JV revenue. All compliant clearing must route through domestic banks with direct SAFE reporting and documentation retention.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is required for the JV legal representative and at least one authorized signatory at the settlement bank branch. The non-resident director may grant a notarized and apostilled power-of-attorney if travel is impossible, but the onshore legal representative must still appear in-branch for the UBO interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted for a newly formed Sino-foreign equity JV under PBOC account-management rules; the bank will require original corporate chops, scanned valid passports, and in-person identity verification for account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk mismatch between an offshore holding structure and the onshore operating JV, with non-resident ultimate beneficial owners controlling Chinese revenue and payroll flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the complete corporate-chain ownership chart with certificates of incorporation and articles of association for every intermediate jurisdiction, notarized passport copies of all natural-person UBOs, board resolutions authorizing the Chinese JV equity investment, audited bank statements and tax records of the investing entity as source-of-funds evidence, and a clear narrative explaining the commercial purpose of the offshore layers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to complete SAFE direct-investment registration before the equity remittance, creating an unregulated inbound capital-account flow that cannot be cleared by any Tier-1 bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the SAFE Foreign Direct Investment registration confirmation certificate, the bank-issued FDI account-opening record, the signed Sino-foreign equity joint venture contract, the JV articles of association, the capital contribution timetable, and an itemized use-of-proceeds statement that matches the declared Chinese corporate income tax classification and SAFE capital-account purpose code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Data-labeling and AI-training services are scrutinized for cross-border data transfer, personal-information exposure, sanctions-adjacent clients, or national-security classification issues by bank compliance committees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a comprehensive privacy and cybersecurity dossier: Personal Information Protection Law impact assessment, Data Security Law classification report, Cybersecurity Law multi-level protection scheme filing, a complete data-processor and client-account roster, contractual AI-training-purpose clauses, a legal opinion from a licensed Chinese cybersecurity law firm confirming lawful data handling, and evidence that no prohibited sensitive data leaves China without government-issued security assessment approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected mass low-value batch payouts to a long-tail annotator and subcontractor pool may mimic layering, mule-account fraud, or sanctions evasion despite the entity's low-risk commercial classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a granular treasury blueprint showing the batch-payment register with full KYC and ID records for each annotator, individual labor or vendor agreements, payroll tax withholding proofs, a specific worker-classification policy, an internal transaction-monitoring program that flags sanctioned persons and abnormal account activity, and a written commitment to monthly suspicious-transaction reporting to the bank and AMLTF.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must remit equity via SWIFT MT103 to the JV's SAFE-monitored FDI capital account at Bank of China or ICBC, with the remittance narrative clearly stating Registered Equity Contribution for a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture. The bank validates the FDI registration certificate, verifies the national unified social credit code, and only converts the inbound USD to CNY after receiving the capital-account income payment instruction letter and performing authenticity review against site leases, payroll schedules, equipment invoices, and other actual transaction documents. All subsequent capital-account payments require matching invoices and SAFE filing records; deregistration and residual capital repatriation require tax clearance and an audit report.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For current-account service payments related to subcontractors, software licensing, and external data-processing support, the JV must use SWIFT MT103 with a service-trade purpose code and submit the underlying contract, invoice, and proof of performance to the settlement bank. For imports of computer hardware or AI-workstation equipment, the JV may use an import Commercial Letter of Credit for high-trust supplier financing, or Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) for lower-risk counterparties. Domestic payroll to Chinese data-labeling staff must be executed through bank-issued batch RMB clearing using exact beneficiary ID numbers; Mass PayPal Payout and Wise are not acceptable clearing rails for the JV's compliance architecture and may only support ancillary disbursements where no foreign exchange or SAFE filing is required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNYUSD deliverable FX forwards executed with a SAFE-designated domestic bank against verifiable current-account receipts or payables
Onshore CNYUSD FX swaps for liquidity conversion maturing in line with the underlying trade or service settlement cycle
Vanilla and zero-premium foreign-exchange options for current-account exposure where the bank establishes genuine economic risk
Cross-currency swaps only with approved capital-account or foreign-debt exposure and after SAFE registration, never for speculative purposes
Non-deliverable forwards are prohibited for onshore entities and may be traded only by non-resident counterparties outside SAFE jurisdiction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise annual information publicity report (Enterprise Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June, Beijing time, for the preceding calendar year; no extension beyond 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing triggers inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations; corrective filing is possible within 3 years; failure to correct within that period results in placement on the List of Seriously Illegal and Dishonest Enterprises, public credit impairment, restrictions on the legal representative's future registrations, and eventual administrative strike-off/revocation of the business license under market-regulation credit supervision procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment information annual report (combined with the enterprise annual report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR jointly with the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the integrated annual reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June for the preceding calendar year; any change in equity ownership or actual controller during the year is additionally reportable within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 15-day administrative rectification order applies for non-reporting or false reporting; continuing non-compliance or material inaccuracy is punishable by statutory administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting rules, entry into abnormal-operation credit records, and increased regulatory scrutiny that can block preferential foreign-investment treatment and delay administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax final settlement and payment return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local competent tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May for the previous calendar year; quarterly provisional prepayments are due by the 15th day of the month following each quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Overdue tax bears a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day from the day after the filing deadline; underpayment or inaccurate filing is subject to administrative penalties ranging from 20%-50% of the short-levied tax, with 50%-5x penalties for fraudulent tax evasion; the tax authority may freeze deposits, seize property, and withhold deregistration/strike-off approval until all tax liabilities are settled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements prepared under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises and approved by the board of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained at the registered office; reported through the SAMR annual report data, submitted to the STA with the annual corporate income tax return when requested, and delivered to the board/shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Board approval must occur no later than 30 March for a 31 December year-end, and the audited financial statements must be completed before the annual CIT settlement deadline of 31 May and before the SAMR annual report deadline of 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare and audit annual financial statements constitutes an accounting and foreign-investment supervision violation; the JV may receive a compliance rectification order, the accounting records may be rejected for tax final settlement purposes, the entity may be listed with abnormal-market-status records, and directors may face personal administrative liability where the failure conceals losses or misleads shareholders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual related-party transaction schedule and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local tax authority through annual CIT return schedules; documentation must be available for desk or field audit inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Related-party schedules are submitted with the annual CIT return by 31 May; the transfer pricing master file and local file must be prepared no later than the same deadline; country-by-country report, if required, is due by 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing or inadequate documentation exposes the JV to transfer pricing tax adjustment, late-payment interest of 0.05% per day on the adjusted tax due, administrative fines for failure to keep compliant books, and potential penalty of 50%-5x of any underpaid tax if the arrangement is treated as tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered office, directors, supervisors, legal representative, and ultimate beneficial controller information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR through the annual information publicity system; beneficial ownership data shared with tax administration and foreign investment supervision authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June for information current as of 31 December; changes during the year are reportable within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or stale public registrations expose the JV to administrative fines, abnormal-operation listing, and cancellation of certain government filing benefits; if the registered address is unreachable and annual returns are not corrected, SAMR may initiate administrative strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Sino-foreign equity joint venture is subject to a mandatory annual independent audit by a certified public accountant registered in the PRC, irrespective of balance sheet size, turnover, or headcount; no size-based audit exemption applies to the JV. In addition, PRC Company Law and regulatory rules compel a certified audit for one-person limited liability companies, listed or public-interest enterprises, financial institutions, and any enterprise whose regulatory license or foreign investor agreement requires audited financial statements. Quantitative regulatory triggers include related-party transaction thresholds that require CPA-supported contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation where annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 40 million for other transaction categories or RMB 100 million for tangible asset, financial asset, and intangible asset transfers; enterprises above those thresholds are also expected to present audited financial statements in the annual CIT final settlement file when the tax authority requests verification.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), which are converged with IFRS; small non-public enterprises may apply the Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises, but the Sino-foreign equity joint venture should use full IFRS-converged CAS for statutory, foreign investment, and consolidated reporting purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not operate a separate public UBO filing form for ordinary non-financial JVs; instead, the annual SAMR/MOFCOM foreign investment information report collects the ultimate controlling party, actual controller, and equity ownership structure as of 31 December. Any transfer of JV equity or change of actual controller during the year must be filed through the foreign investment information reporting system within 30 days of the change. The JV must also maintain an internal beneficial-owner ledger and respond to tax AML beneficial-owner enquiries within the same 30-day window; false or omitted UBO declarations attract foreign-investment reporting fines, abnormal-operation credit listing, and tax-law penalty exposure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers and Encumbrances

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 3,000 per year for a registered office and local corporate agent in tier-1 mainland PRC cities; USD 500 - USD 1,500 per year in second-tier cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 18,000 per year for a JV BPO engaged in AI data labeling, computer vision annotation, and RLHF curation, with upward adjustment for transfer pricing documentation, multi-province payroll, and cross-border payment verification requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Chinese-resident Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is taxed at the statutory 25% headline CIT rate. Preferential reductions may apply if it qualifies as a High and New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) at 15%, or as a Small Low-Profit Enterprise at an effective 5% rate on the first RMB 3 million of annual taxable income. Additional effective-rate stimulants include the 100% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure and accelerated depreciation or inclusion-in-income concessions for software and integrated-circuit enterprises; certain pilot Free Trade Zones such as Hainan Free Trade Port and Shanghai Lingang may apply a 15% encouraged-industry rate where the AI data-labeling BPO qualifies as an encouraged business.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return of the People's Republic of China (A-Class) with attached general and specialized schedules, filed on-line through the State Taxation Administration (STA) e-Tax electronic filing portal or provincial e-Tax bureaus.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual with quarterly or monthly provisional returns during the year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 5 months after the close of the fiscal year-end, no later than May 31 of the following year. Quarterly provisional returns must be filed within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Line 1 - Taxpayer Identification and Fiscal Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Uniform Social Credit Code, legal entity name, registered address, fiscal year start and end dates, and tax registration status of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the JV is a Chinese tax resident by place of incorporation and place of effective management. The JV itself is not a non-resident filer; non-resident shareholders are not registered as CIT filers on the JV's annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 2 - Type of Return and Filing Mode
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicator for annual final settlement, quarterly provisional filing, prior-year adjustment, or special liquidation return; includes classification of the enterprise as general or small low-profit taxpayer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select Annual Final Settlement for Box 2. All schedules are filed on the entity level; non-resident associates are disclosed on the related-party transaction schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 3 - Total Income / Operating Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from AI data labeling, RLHF annotation, computer-vision bounding-box services, and all BPO service fees derived from China and cross-border clients; includes deemed revenue on non-taxable items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the global income of the Chinese resident JV. If the JV has a foreign permanent establishment, foreign-source business profits of a Chinese enterprise are taxable in China unless a foreign tax credit is separately claimed; no credit is mechanically granted on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Line 4 - Deductible Costs, Expenses, and Losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of services, direct labor, software and licensing costs, outsourcing charges to parent or sister companies for data annotation, overhead, and other operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply arm's-length standards to management fees and intercompany service charges payable to a foreign parent. No deduction is allowed for dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders. Accrued but unpaid royalties or interest payable to non-residents are deductible only when the withholding obligation has been lawfully satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 5 - Reconciliation of Accounting Profit to Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for nondeductible related-party charges, over- or under-provisioning, interest on non-enterprise borrowings, tax incentive items, and losses from overseas operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile shared-service charges under CUP or TNMM and ensure that all intercompany allocations are supported by contemporaneous documentation. The non-resident service provider cannot avoid Chinese PE taxation merely by routing through the JV if the charging model lacks economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 6 - Taxable Income after Loss Carryforward and Incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deduction of carryforward losses, reduced by R&D super deduction, and before special free-zone preferential rate computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A JV cannot pass through losses to its non-resident shareholders. Losses must be carried forward within the five-year statutory limit. A deemed permanent establishment of a non-resident provider cannot claim the JV's loss carryforward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Line 7 - Tax Rate, Tax Payable, and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 25% statutory rate, or a 15% preferential HNTE rate or small low-profit rate, to taxable income; compute FIT, foreign tax credit, quarterly prepayments, and total tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Chinese JV, no dividend withholding tax is computed on this line. The withholding obligation on outbound dividend remittance is reported and remitted separately at the time of distribution, not on the JV's CIT return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Line 8 - Special Schedules for Related-Party Transactions and Cross-Border Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach the related-party transaction reporting schedules covering intercompany services, royalty, financing, and equity transfers, and the withholding tax summary for payments to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the beneficial-ownership, Tax Residency Certificate, and treaty-rate claim indicator for every outbound dividend, interest, and royalty. Failure to file these schedules voids treaty relief and converts reduced WHT into a 0.05% per-day late-payment charge plus a 50%-300% penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return is subject to a monetary fine of up to RMB 10,000 under Article 62 of the PRC Tax Administration Law and a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on outstanding tax under Article 32. A false or fraudulent return crosses the criminal threshold when the concealed or omitted tax is RMB 50,000 or more and accounts for more than 10% of the total tax payable; imprisonment can reach three to seven years for a particularly large amount, together with fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10%, withheld at the time the dividend is distributed to a non-resident corporate shareholder; reduced to 5% under most PRC double-tax treaties where the shareholder is the beneficial owner and holds at least a 25% equity interest in the JV for the qualifying period specified in the applicable treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain the reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home-country tax authority, (ii) submit to the JV withholding agent the treaty claim form required by the Chinese tax authority, (iii) establish beneficial ownership by demonstrating that the recipient is not a conduit or agent, (iv) prove the required equity shareholding percentage and holding period under the applicable treaty, and (v) retain all payment, ownership, and contract records for ten years for post-claim audit. A unilateral reduction claimed without prior treaty filing or with a fraudulent TRC will be recharacterized as a misdeclaration, and the under-deducted WHT will be collected from the JV as withholding agent together with a 50%-300% penalty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties and interest paid to a non-resident is 10%. Under DTAs, cross-border interest is commonly reduced to 7%-10% and royalties to 5%-10% depending on the treaty partner and the application of limitation-on-benefits clauses. All payments require the same TRC and beneficial-ownership filing protocol as dividends, with separate justification for royalties based on the actual use of intellectual property in China.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Local File must be prepared where annual related-party transactions exceed the following thresholds in RMB: tangible asset transfers above RMB 200 million, intangible asset transfers above RMB 100 million, financial asset transfers above RMB 100 million, or other related-party transactions above RMB 40 million. A Master File is also required where the MNE group's audited consolidated revenue in the preceding fiscal year is RMB 5 billion or more, and Country-by-Country Reporting is required at the same group-revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The STA applies the economic substance doctrine through Article 41 and Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42. A shell Chinese JV that books profits without performing core income-generating activities, maintaining premises, employees, or risk-management functions in China will be recharacterized as a conduit. In the AI data-labeling context, the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) consist of actual annotation labor, quality-control management, model-training and human-feedback systems, and active servicing contracts. The JV must derive profits in the jurisdiction where the personnel and systems performing those activities are located and cannot be a pure booking company for the foreign partner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-Company Abuse and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Sino-Foreign JV is incorporated in China but has no employees in the data-labeling BPO line, maintains no physical facilities, uses only foreign subcontractors, and allocates nearly all profit overseas while applying a 15% HNTE or free-zone preferential rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under EIT Law Article 47 and Tax Administration Law Article 52, the tax authorities may recharacterize the entity and deny the preferential rate, assess the underpaid CIT at 25%, impose a 0.05% daily surcharge, and levy a fine between 50% and 300% of the underpaid tax under Tax Administration Law Article 63. SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42 additionally requires the filing of a special adjustment report, and the JV may be stripped of its HNTE certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the false related-party disclosure or approve the intercompany allocation will be jointly and severally liable for the CIT underpayment in civil restitution. The legal representative may be placed on the SAT blacklist and banned from leaving China until the tax debt is settled. If the JV's false filings are used to evade tax, directors can face criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment up to three years, and three to seven years for an especially huge amount.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Intercompany Transfer-Pricing Fraud and False TP Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The JV underprices its AI training services to the foreign parent by failing to follow TNMM or CUP, fabricates Local File comparables, inflates offshore royalty or management-fee deductions, and omits related-party transaction schedules on the annual CIT return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax bureau may make a transfer-pricing adjustment under EIT Law Article 41, add an interest adjustment on the under-declared tax, and impose a fraudulent-return penalty of 50% to 300% under Tax Administration Law Article 63. The omission or false filing of related-party transaction schedules is a serious non-filing for which the maximum RMB 10,000 fine under Article 62 is aggravated by the daily late-payment charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who prepare or sign the false TP documentation are personally liable for the tax adjustment to the extent they individually benefitted from the profit shift. A court may pierce the corporate veil under Company Law Article 20, order asset restitution, enforce a travel ban and exit-control order, and impose imprisonment for tax evasion if the adjusted CIT exceeds the criminal threshold and the intent to evade is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Fraudulent DTA Relief on Outbound Dividends
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The JV distributes dividends to a foreign parent while applying the reduced 5% DTA dividend withholding rate without obtaining a Tax Residency Certificate, without proving beneficial ownership, and with the foreign parent immediately back-to-back on-passing the dividend to a zero-tax shell company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The failure to withhold the full 10% statutory tax is a tax-collection violation. Under EIT Law Articles 37 and 38, the JV as withholding agent must pay the uncollected tax plus interest. Under Tax Administration Law Article 69, the JV is fined between 50% and 300% of the amount that should have been withheld. General anti-abuse rules allow the tax bureau to disregard the treaty claim and impose the full 10% rate, or the applicable rate on the actual recipient, plus criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who instruct the CFO to release dividends with a false reduced WHT certificate are jointly liable for the withholding shortfall, as the JV's corporate veil can be pierced for fraudulent under-withholding. The legal representative's personal assets may be used for restitution, the SAT blacklist and travel ban will apply, and under Criminal Law Article 201 the director can face imprisonment of up to seven years and fines if the aggregate fraudulent under-withholding exceeds RMB 50,000 and represents more than 10% of the tax assessed.
